Tournai
toor-NAY
n. (the French-speaking town over whose castle wall the Belgic Confession was thrown to the king's officers in 1561)
French Tournai, Dutch Doornik, from the Celtic turno, a height, with a Latin suffix; the town stands on the Scheldt.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Tournai is the town where a confession of faith was delivered by being thrown over a wall. A French-speaking bishopric on the Scheldt, surrounded by Flemish-speaking country and long disputed between France and the Low Countries, it held from the 1540s one of the most determined Reformed congregations in the Netherlands, served at intervals by Guido de Bres. In September 1561 the congregation marched through the streets at night singing psalms, the demonstrations the authorities called the chanteries, and when the government demanded to know what these people believed, a copy of the newly written Confession of Faith of the Reformed Churches of the Low Countries was thrown over the wall of the castle with a letter addressed to Philip II: a statement that they held the magistrate's authority to be of God and would obey in all things civil, that they numbered many thousands, and that they would not give up the preaching of the word. Repression followed; de Bres fled and was taken six years later. Parma besieged and took the town in 1581, its defence conducted by Christine de Lalaing after her husband left. The dictionary enters Tournai because a confession written for a hostile king and delivered over a wall is the clearest picture of what confessing means.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a confession as a formulary of articles of faith; to confess as to own or acknowledge; a bishopric as the diocese of a bishop; and a demonstration as a public exhibition or show.

expand to see more

CONFESSION, n. A formulary in which the articles of faith are comprised; a public acknowledgment of belief.

CONFESS, v. To own, acknowledge or avow, as a crime, a fault, a charge, a debt or a truth.

BISHOPRIC, n. A diocese; the district over which the jurisdiction of a bishop extends.

DEMONSTRATION, n. The act of demonstrating; a public exhibition or show of feeling or opinion.

WALL, n. A work or structure of stone, brick or other materials, raised to some height, and intended for defense or security.

Key Scripture

Mat 10:32 — "Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven."

Rom 10:10 — "For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation."

1Ti 6:12 — "Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses."

Psa 119:46 — "I will speak of thy testimonies also before kings, and will not be ashamed."

Modern Corruption

French-speaking town on the Scheldt whose Reformed congregation delivered the Belgic Confession over the castle wall to Philip II's officers in 1561.

expand to see more

The corruption to be named is the private faith that will not be stated where it costs something, which the Tournai congregation refused by the manner of its delivery. They did not publish anonymously or petition for tolerance of an unnamed opinion; they wrote out what they believed, article by article, signed it as a body, and handed it to the officers of the king who was executing men for holding it. “Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven” (Mat 10:32) is the warrant, and a confession is the instrument by which a church does it corporately.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the public and verbal nature of faith, which Scripture makes part of salvation's own order: “with the mouth confession is made unto salvation” (Rom 10:10). Timothy is reminded that he “hast professed a good profession before many witnesses” (1Ti 6:12), and the psalmist's resolve is the exact shape of what happened at Tournai: “I will speak of thy testimonies also before kings, and will not be ashamed” (Psa 119:46).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek homologeo (G3670), to confess, to say the same thing; Greek homologia (G3671), a profession; Hebrew edah (H5715), a testimony.

expand to see more

Greek homologeo (G3670) — to say the same thing, to confess openly; “shall confess me before men”, Matthew 10:32.

Greek soteria (G4991) — salvation, deliverance; “with the mouth confession is made unto salvation”, Romans 10:10.

Greek homologia (G3671) — a profession, an open avowal; “hast professed a good profession before many witnesses”, 1 Timothy 6:12.

Hebrew edah (H5715) — a testimony, that which is attested; “I will speak of thy testimonies also before kings”, Psalm 119:46.

Hebrew bosh (H954) — to be ashamed, to be confounded; “and will not be ashamed”, Psalm 119:46.

Usage

"“shall confess me before men” (Mat 10:32) — the Confession thrown over the castle wall, September 1561."

"“I will speak of thy testimonies also before kings, and will not be ashamed” (Psa 119:46) — a letter addressed to Philip II."

"“hast professed a good profession before many witnesses” (1Ti 6:12) — the psalm-singing processions of the chanteries."
